sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management

items.q: Match the laboratory item to the DKA value shown in the table — 1) Glucose 2) Serum sodium 3) Osmolality 4) Plasma ketones … A) 350–1000 mg/dL B) 125–135 mEq/L C) 300–320 mOsm/mL D) ++++
items.exp: The DKA column gives glucose 350–1000, serum sodium 125–135, osmolality 300–320 and plasma ketones ++++. (Book p932)

items.q: What glucose value is printed for HHS in the DKA-versus-HHS table?
items.exp: The HHS glucose row is written as >800 mg/dL. (Book p932)

items.q: The HHS serum-sodium range is 135–145 mEq/L, so the table notes that ___ normal saline is used.
items.exp: The sodium row annotates the HHS 135–145 range with therefore 1/2 NS used. (Book p932)

items.q: Assess the ketone and pH rows: I DKA plasma ketones are ++++. II HHS pH is written as normal.
items.exp: The table shows ++++ plasma ketones for DKA and normal pH for HHS. (Book p932)

items.q: Match the table finding to its DKA direction — 1) Bicarbonate 2) pH 3) PCO2 4) Anion gap … A) Decreased B) Decreased C) Decreased D) Increased
items.exp: The DKA column shows decreased bicarbonate, pH and PCO2, with an increased anion gap. (Book p932)

items.q: A patient has HHS with moderate creatinine increase attributed to fluid loss. Which renal consequence is written beside it?
items.exp: The HHS creatinine cell reads moderate increase with increased fluid loss leading to prerenal failure. (Book p932)

items.q: The first fluid instruction for HHS is slow fluid correction using:
items.exp: HHS management begins with slow fluid correction using 1/2 NS. (Book p932)

items.q: The HHS management note replaces approximately what volume over 4–5 days?
items.exp: The page says replace 12 L over 4–5 days, approximately 3 L/day. (Book p932)

items.q: Assess the insulin transition: I IV insulin is shifted to subcutaneous insulin when the patient is awake and taking fluids. II The page says to stop insulin before the patient can drink.
items.exp: The management arrow says IV insulin, when awake and taking fluids, shifts to subcutaneous insulin. (Book p932)

items.q: Match the subcutaneous insulin item to the printed schedule — 1) Regular insulin 2) Long-acting insulin 3) Ultra-long-acting insulin 4) Normal body production … A) 8 U–8 U–8 U B) Glargine/detemir daily C) Degludec once in two days D) 40 U
items.exp: The overlap note writes 40 U normal production, regular 8–8–8, glargine/detemir daily and degludec once in two days. (Book p932)

items.q: What prognosis is written at the end of the HHS section?
items.exp: The final prognosis line on the page reads relatively poor. (Book p932)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the analytes marked normal in the HHS column?
items.exp: Potassium, magnesium and chloride are marked normal in HHS; plasma ketones are marked ±, not ++++. (Book p932)
